questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a NAND gate?
options: It outputs HIGH only when all its inputs are HIGH.
It outputs LOW only when all its inputs are LOW.
It outputs LOW only when all its inputs are HIGH.
It outputs HIGH if any of its inputs are HIGH.
It outputs HIGH if its inputs are different.

questions.question: In a modern pipelined processor, what is the primary purpose of a branch predictor?
options: To accelerate the fetching of data from main memory by predicting cache misses.
To determine the target address of an indirect jump instruction.
To speculatively guess the outcome of conditional branch instructions to avoid pipeline stalls.
To optimize the allocation of execution units for parallel instruction processing.
To manage the flow of data between different levels of the memory hierarchy.

questions.question: In the context of digital IC verification using simulation, which type of coverage specifically measures whether all specified states, transitions, and sequences of a Finite State Machine (FSM) have been exercised during simulation?
options: Line Coverage
Toggle Coverage
Path Coverage
FSM Coverage
Code Coverage

questions.question: In an out-of-order execution processor, what is the primary role of a 'reservation station' (also known as a scoreboard or instruction queue)?
options: To store completed instructions before they are committed to architectural state.
To track the availability of functional units and operand readiness for instructions awaiting execution.
To predict the outcome of conditional branches to reduce pipeline stalls.
To manage cache coherence among multiple processor cores.
To translate virtual memory addresses to physical memory addresses.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of designing an Integrated Circuit (IC) as a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) compared to a Full Custom Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) for prototyping and low-volume production?
options: FPGAs typically offer significantly higher clock frequencies and lower static power consumption.
FPGAs have much lower Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) costs due to their reconfigurability and lack of custom mask sets.
FPGAs provide a denser and more optimized logic implementation, leading to smaller silicon area.
FPGAs are immune to process variations, ensuring consistent performance across all manufactured units.
FPGAs enable greater analog integration capabilities and specialized mixed-signal functions.
